CEEN 501.title: Energy System Fundamentals
CEEN 501.description: Thermodynamic analysis of energy conversion processes, power cycles and refrigeration cycles. Exergy analysis of conventional energy systems. Thermal conversion technologies.

CEEN 502.title: Alternative Energy Technologies
CEEN 502.description: Factors affecting energy source adoption. Solar, wind, small-scale hydro, tidal, geothermal, electrochemical (batteries, capacitators, and fuel cells), and biochemical energy, electromechanical conversion processes. Energy storage, microgrids, interfacing with main transmissions grids. Techno-economic assessment of alternative energy technologies.

CEEN 503.title: Sustainable Energy Systems
CEEN 503.description: Planetary thermodynamics, energy system evolution, role of renewable energy sources. Alternative energy technologies. Solar, wind, small-scale hydro, tidal, geothermal, and biochemical energy, electromechanical conversion processes. Techno-economic assessment of alternative energy technologies.

CEEN 504.title: Energy Storage and Transmission
CEEN 504.description: Analysis of energy transportation systems from resource extraction to energy services. Thermal, mechanical and electrochemical storage and transport components of electrical and thermal energy systems. Transmission and distribution systems. Distributed generation systems.

CEEN 523.title: Energy and the Environment
CEEN 523.description: Energy/environment/society interactions; development of energy resources; energy demand and its determinants; policy dimension of energy and climate change; impacts on ecosystems; life cycle analysis; impact assessment and other tools for quantitative and qualitative evaluation of alternative energy sources.

CEEN 525.title: Energy Policy
CEEN 525.description: Energy policy process and governance. Sustainable energy as a social and political challenge, formal government structures and process, actors in the policy, policy analysis, policy instrument, and energy planning and approval processes, including environmental assessment. Introduction to demand-side energy policy.

CEEN 550.title: Energy Efficiency and Conservation
CEEN 550.description: Engineering concepts of demand side management (DSM), energy auditing, analysis of buildings and industrial equipment, measurement & verification, and system data analysis. Energy efficient technologies for green buildings and industrial processes. Behavior and energy use. DSM policy concepts.

CEEN 580.title: Directed Studies in Clean Energy Engineering
CEEN 580.description: Work not related to project or thesis.

CEEN 596.title: Project and Report
CEEN 596.description: For M.Eng. students. Carry out a project and prepare an engineering report under the supervision of a faculty member.

CEEN 597.title: Seminar
CEEN 597.description: Presentations and discussions of current topics in the area of Clean Energy Engineering. Pass/Fail.
